study_identification.title: Closing the life-cycle of normative modeling using federated hierarchical Bayesian regression

study_characteristics.study_objective: The paper introduces a federated probabilistic framework using hierarchical Bayesian regression (HBR) to complete the life-cycle of normative modeling. The goal is to estimate a reference normative model across a massive multi-center neuroimaging dataset, learn, update, and adapt the model parameters on decentralized neuroimaging data.

quality_checking.reason: The paper describes the quality control process.
quality_checking.supporting_text: Wehave excluded participants with missing demographic (age/sex) information and those with poor quality imaging data. We excluded 1566 (4%) subjects due to low-quality images. Subjects were excluded if their scan-site median-centered absolute Euler number was higher than 25. The Euler numbers are computed as a part of standard recon-all Freesurfer [54] pipeline. The exclusion of outliers based on Euler numbers has been shown to be a reliable quality control strategy in large neuroimaging cohorts [55, 56]. Median centering is necessary because the Euler number is scaled differently for different datasets. The threshold of 25 was determined empirically by manually examining the excluded scans.

clinical_application_and_analysis.association_analysis: Then, the region-wise areas under the ROC curves (AUCs) are derived to evaluate the predictive power of deviations for each diagnostic label. We employed a conservative approach to testing for statistical significance, where we performed permutation tests with 1000 repetitions and used false discovery rate (FDR) correction [58] to correct for multiple comparisons across 148 regions.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_brief: Our positive experimental results demonstrate the success of hierarchical Bayesian modeling in fulfilling the technical demands for closing the life-cycle of normative modeling.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_detailed: In dementia cases, the best performances are observed in the occipital and temporal lobes... In patients with schizophrenia, our results show the concentration of distinctive areas in the frontal lobe... In early psychosis, only the right middle temporal gyrus (AUC = 0.59) shows significant and stable results.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_limitations: The current implementation of HBR employs a Gaussian likelihood function, hence, assumes a Gaussian distribution for residuals... Another limitation is that models are estimated separately for each brain region without accounting for correlations between brain regions... The quality of scans is a crucial factor in the success of developing a reference normative model.
clinical_application_and_analysis.application_notes: Our contributions pave the way toward incorporating biological measures into the diagnosis and treatment of mental disorders to hopefully find the right treatment at the right time for the right patient.

general_notes.general_notes: The paper proposes a federated learning approach for normative modeling using Hierarchical Bayesian Regression (HBR). This approach is designed to handle multi-site neuroimaging data, addressing challenges like site effects and data privacy. The HBR model is shown to be effective in estimating normative ranges, and it can be extended to new datasets and adapted to local data, making it suitable for real-world clinical applications. The study also demonstrates the potential of this approach for data-driven biomarker discovery in various brain disorders.
